_meta.description: DVP microsimulation calibration data: Gardiner Expressway (km 0) to Hwy 401 (km 15)
_meta.coordinate: NB = northbound (toward Hwy 401, outbound from downtown); SB = southbound (toward Gardiner, inbound to downtown)

corridorWideWeekdayAverage.note: City of Toronto official website states ~135,000 weekday average for the DVP corridor

segmentVariation.note: City of Toronto 2015 tolling study states 110,000 vehicles/weekday north of Bayview Ave interchange (km~3.8). South end near Gardiner sees higher volumes. No single corridor-wide measurement at every km. Ramp cross-street counts provide proxy segment evidence.

northOfBayview_km3p8.source: 2015 Tolling Options study, City of Toronto backgroundfile-83671

southSegmentHigherEstimate.note: South of Bayview (km 0-3.8) estimated 10-20% higher than 110k due to Lake Shore/Gardiner merge traffic

weekdayVsWeekend.note: No direct weekend volume found for DVP mainline in available open data. Most midblock ATR counts are weekday-only 72h studies.

hourlyProfile.dataSource: Combined: Eastern Ave/DVP N Ramp ATR counts 2871386/2871388/2871390 (2021-2023) from Toronto Open Data svc_raw_data_volume_2020_2024.csv; directional split derived from 2001 Toronto Council expansion study cordon count data (published); shape validated against 2017 Bluetooth travel time data
hourlyProfile.note: The Eastern Ave ramp count gives an undirected combined shape for DVP south end (km 0.8). Directional split applied using 2001 cordon ratios: AM peak NB=54%/SB=46%, PM peak NB=49%/SB=51%. CAUTION: This is a ramp-to-arterial count — it captures vehicles using the Queen/Eastern interchange, not total mainline flow. Shape is consistent with Bluetooth speed patterns.

northbound.provenance_detail: Shape from measured Eastern Ave ATR (Toronto Open Data 2021-2023); directional split from published 2001 cordon; combination = estimated
northbound.amPeakHour: 07:00-09:00 (NB also congested in AM per Bluetooth data)

southbound.provenance_detail: Shape from measured Eastern Ave ATR; directional split from published 2001 cordon
southbound.amPeakHour: 07:00-08:00 (SB worst AM congestion: speed drops to 46 km/h at 08:00 per Bluetooth)

peakHourFactorObservation.note: 2001 cordon counts at 401 give ~5,400-6,500 peak-hour volumes per direction. With ~67,500 vehicles/direction/day (135,000/2), the NB AM peak-hour fraction = 6,350/67,500 = 9.4% (1998 data). This is consistent with HCM K-factor range 0.08-0.10 for urban freeways.

dowFactors.dataSource: No direct DVP mainline DOW data found in Toronto Open Data. Values from FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide and HCM typical urban freeway patterns.
dowFactors.source: FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide (2022) Table 4-2: Urban interstate seasonal/DOW patterns. Friday typically 5-8% above weekday average; weekend 20-28% below weekday average for commuter-dominated urban freeways.
dowFactors.note: No measured DOW data found for DVP in Toronto Open Data. Ramp count records are mostly single-week 72-hour captures that do not span full weeks.

observedSpeeds.dataSource: City of Toronto Open Data: Travel Times - Bluetooth (2017 dataset, resource 02e78a5e-cf4f-40b2-91dd-3a454675c3bf from package travel-times-bluetooth). Segments E_F through J_K (NB) and K_J through F_E (SB) identified as DVP mainline (100 km/h design speed per normalDrivingTime field in bluetooth_routes_wgs84.dbf, total ~14.9 km NB = corridor from Gardiner junction to Hwy 401). Weekday averages only (Mon-Fri 2017). Five-minute aggregates averaged by hour of day.
observedSpeeds.caveat: Pre-COVID (2017). Post-COVID volumes recovered to ~pre-COVID by 2024 per Downtown Toronto Congestion Study (Parsons 2024), so 2017 data is a reasonable modern-conditions baseline.

segmentMapping.note: Route IDs from bluetooth_routes_wgs84.dbf (resource f24bd6d6). 100km/h normalDrivingSpeed segments identified as DVP mainline. E=km0 (Gardiner/DVP junction), F=~km2.4, G=~km4.8, H=~km8.5, I=~km11.5, J=~km12.9, K=km15 (Hwy 401). Total corridor: 14.9 km NB / 14.8 km SB.

endToEndTravelTime.note: Calculated from corridor distance ~14.9km / measured corridor speed. 2015 tolling study reported 34 min end-to-end in AM peak direction (no-toll) consistent with measured NB PM data.

segmentSpeeds_hour8_SB.note: Individual segment speeds southbound at 08:00 (worst congestion hour for SB). Segment order: K=km15 to E=km0.

segmentSpeeds_hour17_NB.note: Individual segment speeds northbound at 17:00 (worst congestion hour for NB). Segment order: E=km0 to K=km15.

rampShares.dataSource: Toronto Open Data svc_most_recent_summary_data (resource e90038e7) and svc_summary_data (resource b72cca3a-8190). Ramp cross-street ATR counts from Toronto Open Data midblock dataset. Volumes represent cross-street approach to ramp, not DVP ramp throughput directly.
rampShares.note: DVP ramp throughput is not directly measured in available open data. Values below are ramp terminal cross-street volumes, which are proxies for ramp demand.

rampComponents.note: Eglinton is among the highest-volume interchanges. Cross-street AADT at ramp approaches ~22,000-30,000.
Lawrence is the highest-demand interchange by ramp approach AADT: 45,648 (2020).
Hwy 401 ramp counts are from 2000 — oldest in the dataset. Combined ramp AADT ~51,664.

rankedByRampDemand.note: Ranking from highest to lowest inferred ramp demand, based on cross-street proxy AADT:
ranking: 1. Lawrence Ave E (km 11.8): 45,648 cross-street AADT at ramp approach (2020, measured)
2. Hwy 401 (km 15.0): ~51,664 combined ramp volumes (2000 data, measured but aged)
3. Eglinton Ave E (km 10.0): 25,409 cross-street AADT at ramp approach (2023, measured)
4. Bayview/Bloor (km 3.8): 58,239 at Bloor arterial (arterial AADT not just ramp; measured 2013)
5. Wynford Dr (km 10.7): 14,464 at ramp approach (2023, measured)
6. York Mills Rd (km 14.0): 12,467-14,478 at ramp terminal (2014, measured)
7. Don Mills Rd (km 7.0): 10,412 at ramp terminal (2011, measured)

sources.note: Toronto Open Data: Traffic Volumes - Midblock. Used summary resources (e90038e7, b72cca3a-8190) to find DVP-adjacent ATR count locations, daily volumes, AM/PM peak hours and volumes for all DVP-adjacent counts.

Toronto Open Data: Raw 15-minute volume data 2020-2024. Downloaded (2.5MB) and parsed. Found 3 Eastern Ave/DVP N Ramp counts (2871386/2871388/2871390, 2021-2023) providing measured undirected hourly volume shape.

Toronto Open Data: Travel Times - Bluetooth. Downloaded 2017 dataset (resource 02e78a5e, 1.8MB compressed). Downloaded route shapes (resource f24bd6d6). Parsed DBF and CSV. Identified DVP as segments E-K (~14.9km). Computed corridor and segment average speeds by hour on weekdays.
City of Toronto DVP page. Source for 135,000 weekday average statistic and basic corridor facts.

City of Toronto 2015 Tolling Options study. Source for: 110,000 vehicles/weekday north of Bayview; AM peak no-toll travel time 34 min and avg speed 26 km/h; both-direction peak congestion characterization.

City of Toronto 2001 DVP Expansion proposal. Source for: peak-hour cordon counts at Hwy 401 (1987-1998 series); directional split: NB AM 6,350 / SB AM 5,410 (1998); design capacity ~1,600 veh/hr/lane; outbound-dominant AM flow interpretation.

dataGaps.detail: No count records with location matching DVP mainline (not ramp) found in Toronto Open Data midblock counts. All ATR counts are on ramp connections to cross-streets or cross-street approaches. Directional mainline volumes by hour are not available in open data.
dataGaps.workaround: Bluetooth travel times for speed; Eastern Ave ramp ATR for volume shape; 2001 cordon for directional split

dataGaps.detail: Confirmed deprecated/inactive by user. Not attempted.
Open data portal only has 2014-2017 Bluetooth data. 2017 dataset used as most recent available.
dataGaps.workaround: 2017 data used; pre-COVID conditions. Post-COVID recovery confirmed to match pre-COVID levels per Parsons 2024 study.

dataGaps.detail: No weekend ATR count found for DVP mainline or adjacent ramps in available open data.

dataGaps.item: Lake Shore/Don Roadway and Danforth interchange ramp volumes
dataGaps.detail: No ATR count records found for km 0.0 and km 2.7 interchanges in available data.
dataGaps.workaround: Inferred as lower-demand based on absence and low volumes at nearby km 0.8-1.6 interchanges

dataGaps.item: Directional hourly volume fractions (NB and SB separately)
dataGaps.detail: Eastern Ave ramp count is a single direction on a one-way ramp. True bidirectional mainline hourly counts do not exist in open data. The hourly profile is estimated by applying a directional split (from 2001 cordon) to the undirected ramp count shape.
dataGaps.workaround: Bluetooth speed data independently validates the shape: both directions show AM congestion, NB shows strong PM congestion, consistent with estimated volume distribution
